status_definitions.supported: Evidence supports the stated direction, sign, and reasoning within the declared scope.
status_definitions.partially_supported: Evidence supports only part of the claim, a narrower population or outcome, or an association rather than the full causal claim.
status_definitions.contradicted: Relevant evidence opposes the claimed direction or sign within the declared scope.
status_definitions.mixed_evidence: Relevant evidence both supports and opposes the same defined claim.
status_definitions.insufficient_evidence: Available evidence does not establish or refute the causal claim.
status_definitions.not_assessable: Undefined variable coding or endpoint makes the proposed direction or sign uninterpretable.

methodology.scope: 2010_32 yo.py, 62 edges, using only the 25 supplied PDF files in 2010 ADHD Papers (24 unique documents; one exact duplicate). Direction, sign, and written reasoning were reviewed; numeric strength was excluded.
methodology.age_scope: Adult evidence was required for adult claims. Young-adult and general-adult evidence was treated as partial when it did not report an age-32 estimate. Pediatric findings were not transferred as adult causal proof.
methodology.causal_standard: Associations, reviews, and clinical recommendations were not automatically treated as proof of causal direction. Undefined categorical signs were marked not_assessable.
methodology.source_limits: This is a validation against the supplied corpus, not a systematic review of all 2010 ADHD literature. A status of insufficient_evidence is not evidence that an edge is false.
methodology.strength: The graph's numeric edge strengths were not validated.
methodology.duplicate: s12402-010-0036-9 (1).pdf is byte-identical to s12402-010-0036-9.pdf and was counted once as a unique document.

edges.existing_reasoning: Genetic vulnerability contributes to adult ADHD.
edges.observation_from_validation: Adult and genetic reviews describe ADHD as highly heritable and persistent from childhood. The graph's generic liability claim is better supported than any specific variant mechanism.
edges.recommended_action: Retain the positive edge, define Genetic Risk as aggregate inherited liability, and avoid implying a known single variant.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Although twin and family studies have shown attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) to be highly heritable, genetic variants influencing the trait at a genome-wide significant level have yet to be identified.
evidence.relevance: Supports inherited liability while cautioning that individual genome-wide significant variants were not identified.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Adult individuals with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) have been suffering from this neurobiological and highly heritable disorder chronically since childhood.
evidence.relevance: Supports persistence into adulthood and inherited liability, but does not provide an age-32-specific estimate.

edges.existing_reasoning: Underlying ADHD increases adult symptom severity.
edges.observation_from_validation: ADHD and Symptom Severity overlap unless ADHD is defined as a latent liability separate from diagnostic symptoms.
edges.recommended_action: Define separate latent and measured constructs before assigning a signed causal edge.

edges.existing_reasoning: ADHD shapes inattentive, hyperactive, or combined presentation.
edges.observation_from_validation: Symptom Type is categorical and has no ordered scale, so a universal positive sign is undefined.
edges.recommended_action: Use subtype-specific outcomes or an unsigned relationship.

edges.existing_reasoning: ADHD commonly co-occurs with anxiety, mood, or learning difficulties.
edges.observation_from_validation: The adult review reports frequent psychiatric comorbidity, but co-occurrence does not establish ADHD as its cause.
edges.recommended_action: Represent this as an association or specify a comorbid outcome and causal mechanism.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Furthermore, a large part of this population suffers from psychiatric comorbidity.
evidence.relevance: Supports adult co-occurrence, not ADHD causing each comorbid condition.

edges.existing_reasoning: At age 32, overt hyperactivity may reduce but inattentive impairment can remain.
edges.observation_from_validation: Young adults with lifetime ADHD may fall below full symptom criteria while retaining elevated symptoms. This is consistent with attenuation and persistence, but does not estimate an age-to-severity effect at 32.
edges.recommended_action: Retain a qualified developmental trajectory rather than a fixed negative linear edge.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Although they may no longer meet the full symptom criterion, young adults with a history of lifetime DSM-IV-like ADHD maintain higher levels of ADHD symptoms compared to the general population.
evidence.relevance: Supports symptom persistence with attenuation in young adults, but not a causal estimate at age 32.

evidence.exact_excerpt: Lower male:female ratios than reported in some clinic-based studies suggest that females are under-diagnosed in the community.
